artwork.prompt: Create one photorealistic portrait 2:3, full-bleed documentary photograph for one small crop-rotation inset in The Vegetable Guru, about 16 mm wide in print. The main vegetable must be readable instantly at that size. Match natural bright overcast Cornish daylight, restrained truthful green and earth colours, gently lifted shadows, lightly blurred surroundings and ordinary home-grown produce. One simple focal area, sufficient clear tonal separation around it, a little breathing room, no harsh deep shadows, saturated cartoon colours, black borders, styled studio scene, text, graphics, people, hands, clothing or tools. Photo only. Photograph a close cluster of three fresh shelling pea pods, visibly from a real garden pea (Pisum sativum): look like the author's real peas in the first reference. The second, an actual freshly opened pod, shows spherical peas in their natural single row. Two full plump smooth curved green pods with visible pea bulges on living vine, and one pod recently opened along its seam so four or five tightly seated round green peas face camera and read at a glance; the two halves must have convincing pea pod anatomy. Keep the pods dominant across the central 70–80 percent of the frame, mostly at a gentle diagonal and in one tight cluster, with only a few soft tendrils and round pea leaflets. The darker and more distant background is recognisably an allotment pea bed but subdued and about one stop darker than the subject. No prominent lattice, busy tangles, senescent beige pod, oversized peas, duplicated pod outlines, or other crop. Show the open pod as the clearest motif.

Create one photorealistic portrait 2:3, full-bleed documentary photograph for one small crop-rotation inset in The Vegetable Guru, about 16 mm wide in print. The main vegetable must be readable instantly at that size. Match natural bright overcast Cornish daylight, restrained truthful green and earth colours, gently lifted shadows, lightly blurred surroundings and ordinary home-grown produce. One simple focal area, sufficient clear tonal separation around it, a little breathing room, no harsh deep shadows, saturated cartoon colours, black borders, styled studio scene, text, graphics, people, hands, clothing or tools. Photo only. Photograph one clearly headed green cabbage growing in the soil in a Cornish allotment. First reference is John's actual cabbage plant and gives natural overlapping waxy leaves and green colour. Choose a slightly higher, close three-quarter camera angle to show one unmistakably round dense pale green head surrounded by only a few darker splayed wrapper leaves, pale branching veins and slight natural imperfections. The head fills about two-thirds of width, remains clear and distinct from the outer leaf rosette and has gentle shape shading, a small bit of soil around base, no insect or disease emphasis. The second photograph ref is only for the allotment soil and muted ground texture. Keep the plant itself full of detail and remove background clutter, mesh, bottles, canes, competing crops and cut edges on the central head. Ordinary round UK summer or autumn green cabbage, visibly tight-headed rather than a loose kale, lettuce, cauliflower rose or brassica seedling.

Match natural bright overcast Cornish daylight, restrained truthful green and earth colours, gently lifted shadows, lightly blurred surroundings and ordinary home-grown produce. One simple focal area, sufficient clear tonal separation around it, a little breathing room, no harsh deep shadows, saturated cartoon colours, black borders, styled studio scene, text, graphics, people, hands, clothing or tools. Photo only. Photograph two freshly lifted orange carrots lying diagonally on the crumbly dark soil of John's home garden, long tips pointing toward the lower left. Crop references 1 and 2 establish genuine homegrown carrot anatomy, natural light soil marks, surface colour and fine foliage. Reference 3 is only for the garden and soil style. Frame close, each orange taproot easily legible, one large straightforward broad-shouldered tapered carrot and a slightly shorter uneven one angled just a little apart, and a small attached tuft of real finely divided carrot tops. Make the orange root bodies the strongest motif and keep both the crowns and tips within the portrait safe field. Add small realistic soil flecks rather than rinsed supermarket gloss or a thick mask of mud. Leave some soil dark around the roots for clear contrast and a softly blurred out-of-focus bed behind. Only carrots and soil, no beetroot from the reference, no face, hands or part of a person.
